title: Quarterly capacity quadrant: Dedicated autoscale roadmap & OKR orchestration
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Objective: Produce a compact, operational quarterly roadmap that maps dedicated pool capacity across four operational quadrants (regional tiers x customer commitment tiers), aligns to org OKRs for autoscale cost/reliability, and defines tangible runbook + evaluation deliverables for the next cycle.

Context: We repeatedly see edge cases when routing and burst policies interact with reserved pools (cross-region failover, FaaS-like burst lanes, and fractional-shares billing). This ticket consolidates a single source-of-truth for the next quarter that: (1) slices capacity by quadrant (NA/EU x Gold/Silver Bronze commitment tiers), (2) defines per-quadrant SLOs and capacity corridors, (3) specifies experiments and gating criteria for autoscale behaviors, and (4) ties acceptance criteria to OKRs (cost per 1M tokens, 99.95% availability for P95 requests, and median tail latency improvement).

Scope (what we will deliver):
- Quarter roadmap doc with quadrant maps and prioritized initiatives (policy, telemetry, cost experiments).
- Cross-team OKR spreadsheet linking initiative to engineering milestones and PM success metrics.
- Release plan for two canaries: a prewarm/corridor canary for committed pools, and a burst-reservoir canary for best-effort tiers.
- Runbook templates for fast rollback and capacity hedging with explicit trigger thresholds.
- Measurement dashboard queries (Console) for signal contracts: pool utilization, allocation drift, prewarm hit-rate, p95 latency, and cost-per-token.

Out of scope: Model-level kernel tuning, private deployment installation packaging, billing pricing model rewrite. Those have separate initiatives.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Roadmap doc approved by Eng leads (runtime + infra) and GTM.
2) OKR spreadsheet contains measurable targets and owners for each initiative.
3) Canary runbook and rollback thresholds are documented and linked to a CI job.
4) Dashboard panels for the five signal-contract metrics exist in Console preview and return sane historical baselines.
5) Executive one-pager summarizing cost impact and worst-case rollback plan prepared for leadership review.
metrics: p95 latency target <= 180ms for committed pools
Cost per 1M tokens reduced by 7% in pilot quadrants
Pool utilization target 65-85% in steady state
risks: Overcommitting pools increases idle costs if forecasts are wrong
Canary failure could double request latencies in a region without automated fallback
Telemetry gaps: missing signals will block gating criteria
Cross-region data transfer cost spike in stress scenarios
